subject: Private deployment: patch escrow & contingency coordination
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Tim O'Neal <tim.oneal@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, ACME Health IT <acme-support@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment: patch escrow & contingency coordination

Hi Tim —

Thanks again for walking through the Private upgrade constraints yesterday. Based on our follow-up engineering review I wanted to propose a concrete plan and surface a few decisions we need from ACME before we lock windows. Key points below — full draft attached (maintenance-plan-v2.pdf) and a CSV rollback checklist for your ops team.

Summary proposal (short):
- Version strategy: we recommend pinning the customer fleet to v3.1.4 for production during the weekend window, with a staged canary on a 5% slice in your staging VPC 72 hours prior.
- Patch escrow: Redwood will hold a short-lived rollback image (v3.1.3) in the escrow registry tier for 14 days post-upgrade. If critical regressions appear we will re-pin automatically within the rollback SLA window.
- Maintenance windows: two options — (A) weekend narrow window: Sat 02:00–05:00 PT (minimal traffic) or (B) nightly micro-window over three nights 01:00–02:00 PT with slice-by-slice cutover. Please pick preferred cadence.
- Rollback gating: automatic >50% error-rate or >20s P95 latency sustained for 5 minutes triggers auto-fallback. Manual abort available from your on-call.

Questions for ACME (explicit asks):
1) Confirm preferred window option (A or B) and blackout constraints for the month of Dec.
2) Approval for Redwood-managed rollback escrow image retention for 14 days. ACME can opt for shorter retention if preferred.
3) Any procurement/SOC2 evidence needed for the escrow process (we can surface image attestations and audit logs).

Operational notes for ACME NOC:
- We will provide a pre-signed canary snapshot and a dry-run playbook for your ops (see rollback-checklist.csv).
- KV/State concerns: in-place pinning will flush ephemeral KV caches; long-lived session tokens are unaffected. Recommended pre-cutover drain: 10 minutes per slice.

Next steps:
- If we get window confirmation by Friday EOD we will schedule the canary and run the dry-run with your staging team next Tuesday.

Attaching: maintenance-plan-v2.pdf (full timeline + risk matrix) and rollback-checklist.csv (play-by-play).

Thanks —
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

- Window: prefer option (A) the single narrow weekend window (Sat 02:00–05:00 PT) — helps limit change windows during business hours.
- Escrow image retention: 14 days is fine; procurement will want a short note for the contract addendum.
- SOC2/evidence: please attach the image attestation doc and the audit-log extract for the canary run.

Two operational asks:
1) Can you confirm the exact steps for session draining? We need the NOC playbook bullet list to hand to our on-call.
2) For canary: can we run the 5% slice for 48 hours (rather than 72)? If telemetry looks clean we can sign off earlier.

Naomi / Karthik —

A few engineering clarifications to include in the NOC playbook and the rollback-checklist.csv:

Pre-cutover (staging):
- Snapshot: take image snapshot s3://acme-private-snapshots/20261029-canary-1 before any migration artifacts.
- KV Cache: drain traffic to canary slice for 30 minutes, then run cache-validate (script attached in the plan).
- Telemetry hooks: enable token-level tracing + latency buckets for the canary.

During cutover (production window):
- Slice scheduling: drain -> cut -> validate -> monitor (10m drain, 15m validation, 30m monitor per slice).
- Circuit-breaker: if P95 increases >20s or error-rate >50%, flip circuit and start re-pin within 3 minutes. Re-pin is an automated job that re-applies v3.1.3 image tag to the fleet segment.
- DB migrations: none required in this patch; if that changes we will abort.

Rollback specifics:
- Escrow image pull: registry.redwood.ai/acme/escrow/v3.1.3:pull-manifest will be available; we will provide signed manifest + attestation.
- Snapshot restore path: restore node snapshot, clear ephemeral caches, and reintroduce traffic slice-by-slice.

I added concrete CLI lines in the attached rollback-checklist.csv for the NOC. Also added a step to capture Redb logs (redb.dump) for the 15 minutes preceding any auto-fallback.

Let me know if ACME needs a dry-run runbook with commands expanded.

-Monica
Monica Patel
